reason: Strassen has the largest potential change to n=512 work, but its FP32 accuracy and timed data-movement costs are unverified. Rank its shared-workspace schedule next; combining three allocations into one may save little beside seven subproducts. The one-level fast-path proposal overlaps that same Strassen design. Fused transpose and smaller-panel packing could reduce scratch traffic, with substantial implementation and correctness risk. The remaining proposals have limited evidence for n=512: prior schedule and scratch-lifetime candidates did not promote, tail and C fallback changes target other sizes, and SME tile reassignment may compile to equivalent behavior. The paired-load proposal has unresolved instruction legality, so it ranks last.
